messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High severity - 5 nodes in inferpool-usw became NotReady within 2m, multiple serving containers restarted, elevated OOM/sigkill observed. Auto-evac triggered. https://internal.incident/6998877001 :rotating_light:
jen: I'm on it, looking at the alert graph now. Seeing a spike in kubelet restarts and cgroup OOMs tied to /run/redwood/runtime.
vikram: I can take initial triage. @jen which customer queues are impacted?
sara: Canary says ~12% of hosted requests got 503s over the last 90s, mostly seq-length > 1024. A few customers reported elevated latency via support.
alice: grabbing node list: `kubectl get nodes -l pool=infer-usw -o wide`
alice: ```
NAME                         STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
infer-usw-028.internal       NotReady    <none>   34d   v1.27.3
infer-usw-029.internal       NotReady    <none>   34d   v1.27.3
infer-usw-030.internal       NotReady    <none>   34d   v1.27.3
...
```
ben: logs from runtime on infer-usw-029 show repeated `OOMKilled` in the serving runtime and then a container restart loop.
ben: ```
2026-03-17T12:10:04 runtime[pid=742]: allocation failed: out of memory
2026-03-17T12:10:04 kernel: Killed process 742 (runtime) total-vm:...
2026-03-17T12:10:05 kubelet[...]: Container runtime restarting container
```
miguel: GPU driver messages interleaved, `NVRM: Xid (23):` in dmesg for 028 and 030. Looks like a driver fault during heavy decode.
vikram: ok, plan: 1) cordon the NotReady nodes (if not already), 2) increase fallback routing weight to dedicated-usw for the next 15m, 3) escalate to eng-runtime for kernel/GPU trace, 4) start draining one node at a time to avoid mass eviction.
jen: I'm toggling routing now: `sh /ops/bin/traffic-shift --from=infer-usw --to=dedicated-usw --pct=30 --duration=15m`  :white_check_mark:  Shift applied, monitoring.
sara: posting a quick customer update to status page: "Intermittent inference errors and latency for some hosted customers in US-West. We've shifted traffic to redundant capacity and are investigating"
eng-runtime-bot: @eng-runtime incident 6998877001 created, attaching runtime traces request. Priority: P1.
ben: while draining infer-usw-029 I see pod eviction failing due to stale PV detach timeout. Trying `kubectl drain infer-usw-029 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` now.
alice: note: autoscaler is queued but cold-start for large models will add latency. We should keep fallback weight conservative.
miguel: I've pulled NVML logs and uploading to the incident folder. Initial look: repeated ECC errors before driver reset on 030.
vikram: eng-runtime — can you confirm whether this matches the regression we patched last week? @eng-runtime
eng-runtime-bot: Eng-runtime pinged. Suspected regression flagged; attaching runbook section: "GPU-driver-reset-handling" and requesting debug kernel logs from nodes.
jen: current metrics: errors dropping to ~3% since traffic shift. No new NotReady nodes. Continuing stepwise drains, one node at a time, and keeping support informed.
vikram: if drains complete cleanly, we'll uncordon and roll kubelet with the watchdog fix. If driver faults persist, we'll open vendor ticket with cloud provider.
sara: I'm prepping a short postmortem doc stub with timeline and customer impact counts. Will update with root cause when eng-runtime confirms. :memo:
ben: will keep an eye on PV detach errors — rescheduling of large-model-serving pods is the slow part.
jen: thanks team — ping me in this thread for any blocking items. :thumbsup:
